answer: We formulate dynamic opportunity-cost bonds $B(\theta)$ integrated with zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs generated by ferrous sensor arrays positioned across a karst ridge. By subjecting identities to a subgame-perfect slashing matrix $\mathbf{S}$, the expected payoff of generating $n$ Sybil clones reduces to $E[U(n)] = \pi(n) - n \cdot B(\theta) - \mathbf{S}(n) < 0$ for all $n \ge 2$. Hence, identity multiplication is strictly dominated, converging the multi-agent system to a robust Nash equilibrium where capital barriers completely neutralize adversarial utility.
